title: ConfigProvider
description: Provides the theme and the language of the React library to your application, and exposes them through useConfig().

usage.title: Usage
usage.text: Render one ConfigProvider at the root of your application. It applies the theme as CSS variables on <html>, sets the language of the React library's built-in texts, and provides both to useConfig().
usage.dynamic: Both props are reactive: store them in state to let users switch theme or language at runtime.
usage.global: Only the outermost ConfigProvider touches global state: it writes data-theme, data-palette and the theme variables on <html>, persists the cookies and sets the React library's global language. A nested provider never does; it scopes its own settings to its subtree (see Nesting providers).

palette.title: Palette, persistence and callbacks
palette.text: palette adds a color palette ("editorial", "tech", "graphite" or "cool") on top of the light, dark or system theme. persist saves theme and palette changes in the theme and palette cookies and restores them after hydration. onThemeChange and onPaletteChange are called after setTheme and setPalette change the value.
palette.setters: useConfig() also returns mode, resolvedMode and palette, and the setTheme and setPalette setters, so any component can switch the theme without lifting state. Server rendering, cookies and the no-flash init script are covered in

brand.title: Brand color
brand.text: primaryColor sets your brand color without overriding --primary-color by hand: pass a CSS color ("#4f46e5", rgb(), a named color) for both modes, or a { light, dark } pair. It keeps the explicit theme: theme stays "light", "dark" or "system", so data-theme, useConfig().mode and ThemeToggle keep working.
brand.derive: Derived tokens: every token derived from primary-color (hover, active, subtle, border, text, focus ring, selected color and, unless the palette has its own, the accent tokens) is recomputed from the brand color with the default theme's formulas. A single color gets a dark-mode value mixed toward white in OKLab until it reaches a 4.5:1 contrast on dark surfaces (#4f46e5 becomes #7b85f2); colors that already pass are kept.
brand.precedence: Precedence: primaryColor wins over the primary color of the palette and of the theme; the palette keeps its other tokens. An invalid color is ignored, with a warning in development.
brand.nesting: Nesting: nested providers inherit the brand color, and a nested primaryColor applies to its subtree only (including its overlays); null restores the theme's own primary color.
brand.ssr: Server rendering: the root provider renders the light and dark brand values in a <style> keyed on data-theme, so the server markup has the brand color before hydration (no flash with the theme init script). React Native (MinervaProvider), Taro, uni-app and WeChat mini program providers (ConfigProvider / ThemeProvider), Vue (ConfigProvider / ThemeProvider), Angular (<mn-config primaryColor>, provideMinerva({ primaryColor })) and <minerva-config primary-color> accept the same value, with the same semantics.

context.title: ConfigContext
context.text: useConfig() throws when there is no ConfigProvider above it, which catches setup mistakes early. Read ConfigContext directly when the provider is optional: it returns undefined instead of throwing.

nesting.title: Nesting providers
nesting.text: A ConfigProvider inside another one is a nested provider. Use it to give one region of the page, a preview or a demo another theme, palette or language without affecting the rest of the page.
nesting.inherit: Inheritance: it inherits theme, palette and locale from the closest provider above it. Only the props you set are overridden, and useConfig() below it returns the merged values. Inherited settings keep following the parent when it changes.
nesting.scoped: Scoped theme: a theme or palette override applies to its subtree only. The provider renders a wrapper element with display: contents (so the layout does not change) that carries data-theme, data-palette and the theme variables. Without a theme or palette override, no wrapper is rendered.
nesting.locale: Scoped language: a locale override only changes the built-in texts of its subtree. A provider that only sets locale never touches the theme.
nesting.portal: Overlays: content rendered in a portal from a scoped subtree (Modal, Drawer, Popover, Select, Menu, Tooltip, Toast…) goes into a container on <body> that carries the same scope, so overlays get the scoped theme too. Imperative APIs rendered outside the React tree, such as a standalone confirm(), use the root theme.
nesting.document: Global state: a nested provider never writes to <html>, never reads or writes the cookies (persist is ignored) and never changes the React library's global language. Unmounting it leaves the page exactly as the root provider set it, and unmounting the root provider restores what it changed. setTheme and setPalette of a nested provider change its own override, or the parent's value for a setting it does not override.

props.name: theme
props.description: Theme to apply: "auto" (follows `prefers-color-scheme`), a built-in theme name, a theme object, or a `{ light, dark }` pair. The root provider applies it to `<html>`; a nested provider inherits its parent's theme unless set, and applies an override to its own subtree only.

props.name: palette
props.description: Palette applied with the light / dark / system themes ("editorial", "tech", "graphite", "cool"); `null` keeps Minerva's default look. The root provider sets `data-palette` on `<html>`; a nested provider inherits its parent's palette unless set, and scopes an override to its subtree. Palette tokens come from `style.css`.

props.name: primaryColor
props.description: Brand color: sets `--primary-color` and recomputes every token derived from it (hover, active, subtle, border and text roles, selected, focus ring, and the accent when the palette has no accent of its own) with the default theme's formulas, without changing the light / dark mode. A single color applies to light mode and gets a dark-mode value lightened for contrast on dark surfaces (WCAG 4.5:1); pass `{ light, dark }` to choose both. Wins over the primary color of the theme and of the palette. Accepts hex, `rgb()` / `rgba()` and the basic named colors; an invalid value is ignored (development warning). A nested provider inherits its parent's brand color unless set (`null` restores the theme's own), and scopes an override to its subtree.

props.name: persist
props.description: Persist theme and palette changes in the `theme` / `palette` cookies and restore them after hydration (pair with `THEME_INIT_SCRIPT` for SSR). Root provider only: ignored by nested providers.

props.name: locale
props.description: Language of the React library's built-in texts. The root provider sets it globally; a nested provider inherits its parent's language unless set, and applies an override to its subtree only.

props.name: preset
props.description: Design preset: a named combination of the design axes below and a default palette. "minerva" (default look), "editorial" (restrained, reading-oriented: editorial palette, comfortable density, small radius, subtle shadows, large type), "compact" (dense, data-heavy screens) or "touch" (consumer mobile apps: comfortable density, 44px touch targets, large radius). Explicit axes and `palette` win over the preset. A nested provider inherits its parent's design unless set; a nested preset resets every axis it does not set.

props.name: density
props.description: Spacing density of controls (heights, paddings) and rows (menus, lists, tables): `data-density`

props.name: radius
props.description: Corner radius scale (`--radius-sm` ... `--radius-2xl`): `data-radius`

props.name: shadow
props.description: Elevation shadows (`--shadow-sm` ... `--shadow-xl`): `data-shadow`. "standard" keeps the theme / palette shadows

props.name: fontScale
props.description: Type scale (`--font-size-*`, line heights): `data-font-scale`. "large" is reading-oriented

examples.title: Brand color
examples.description: Nested ConfigProviders with primaryColor in the site's current mode: indigo as a single color (dark value derived), as a { light, dark } pair, and teal. Switch the site theme to compare the derived dark values.

examples.title: Custom theme
examples.description: A custom theme built from themes.light and passed to a nested ConfigProvider: only this container is re-themed, including the Select menu rendered in a portal.

examples.title: Locale
examples.description: A nested ConfigProvider that only sets locale (en, zh, ja or fr): the built-in texts of its subtree change, while the theme and palette are inherited from the site and <html> is left untouched.

examples.title: Palettes
examples.description: Each card is a nested ConfigProvider with its own palette, in the site's current mode. The site's root provider keeps data-palette on <html>.

examples.title: Reading the configuration
examples.description: useConfig() returns the configured theme, the resolved theme, the palette and the locale of the nearest provider. Change the site theme, palette or language in the header to see it update.

ConfigContextProviderProps.theme: Theme to apply: "auto" or its alias "system" (follows prefers-color-scheme), a built-in theme name, a theme object, or a { light, dark } pair. The root provider applies it to <html>; a nested provider inherits its parent's theme unless set, and applies an override to its own subtree only.
ConfigContextProviderProps.palette: Palette applied with the light, dark and system themes ("editorial", "tech", "graphite", "cool"); null keeps Minerva's default look. The root provider sets data-palette on <html>; a nested provider inherits its parent's palette unless set, and scopes an override to its subtree. The palette tokens come from style.css.
ConfigContextProviderProps.primaryColor: Brand color: a CSS color for both modes (the dark-mode value is derived for contrast on dark surfaces) or a { light, dark } pair. Recomputes every token derived from primary-color and wins over the palette's primary color, keeping the explicit light / dark mode. A nested provider inherits it unless set and scopes an override to its subtree; null restores the theme's own. Invalid colors are ignored with a development warning.
ConfigContextProviderProps.persist: Persist theme and palette changes in the theme and palette cookies and restore them after hydration (pair it with THEME_INIT_SCRIPT for SSR). Root provider only: nested providers ignore it.
ConfigContextProviderProps.onThemeChange: Called after setTheme changes the theme.
ConfigContextProviderProps.onPaletteChange: Called after setPalette changes the palette.
ConfigContextProviderProps.locale: Language of the React library's built-in texts. The root provider sets it globally; a nested provider inherits its parent's language unless set, and applies an override to its subtree only.
ConfigContextProviderProps.preset: Design preset: a named combination of the design axes and a default palette ("minerva", "editorial" for a restrained, reading-oriented look, "compact" for dense screens, "touch" for consumer mobile apps). Explicit axes and palette win over it. See Design presets.
ConfigContextProviderProps.density: Spacing density of controls and rows (data-density).
ConfigContextProviderProps.shadow: Elevation shadow scale (data-shadow); "standard" keeps the theme / palette shadows.

ConfigContextProps.theme: Theme as configured (may be "auto" or a { light, dark } pair).
ConfigContextProps.resolvedTheme: Theme currently applied after resolving "auto" and { light, dark } pairs: a built-in theme name or a theme object.
ConfigContextProps.locale: Current locale of the React library's built-in texts.
ConfigContextProps.mode: Color mode of the theme: "light" or "dark" for those themes, "system" for "auto", "system" and { light, dark } pairs, undefined for other themes.
ConfigContextProps.resolvedMode: Applied color mode (data-theme on <html>, or on the scope element of a nested provider), when it can be determined.
ConfigContextProps.palette: Active palette (data-palette on <html>, or on the scope element of a nested provider), null for Minerva's default look.
ConfigContextProps.primaryColor: Brand color applied to the subtree as a { light, dark } pair (the dark value derived when a single color was given), null when the theme's own primary color is used.
ConfigContextProps.setTheme: Changes the theme (saved to the theme cookie when persist is on).
ConfigContextProps.setPalette: Changes the palette (saved to the palette cookie when persist is on).
ConfigContextProps.design: Resolved design axes (preset, density, radius, shadow, fontScale) applied to <html> or to the scope of a nested provider.

Locale.language: Language of the React library's built-in texts: "en", "zh", "ja" or "fr".

basic.title: Basic usage
basic.description: <minerva-config> renders as display: contents and scopes the theme of everything inside it: here one light and one dark scope side by side.

palette-design.title: Palette and design
palette-design.description: palette, design (preset) and the density / radius / shadow / font-scale overrides apply to the subtree only.

locale.title: Locale
locale.description: locale sets the language of the built-in texts of the elements inside (pagination total, empty state). Change it to see them update live.

nested.title: Nested scopes and theme events
nested.description: Scopes nest and the closest one wins: the inner scope stays light while the outer one follows the buttons. minerva-theme-change reports the resolved mode, also for theme="system".

brand-color.title: Brand color
brand-color.description: Scopes with primary-color: indigo as a single color (dark value #7b85f2 derived), indigo in a dark scope, and teal winning over the editorial palette primary.

props.root: Writes the attributes on <html> (whole page) instead of this subtree.

events.minerva-theme-change: The resolved light / dark mode changed (detail: { mode }), e.g. the system preference with theme="system".

switching.title: Switching themes
switching.description: Switching themes using MinervaProvider; the preview follows the selected site theme and palette.

use-theme.title: Using theme tokens
use-theme.description: Using theme tokens using MinervaProvider; the preview follows the selected site theme and palette.
